from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Diffusion Models", [
            "Diffusion models learn to reverse Gaussian noise.",
            "Images dissolve into pure random noise states.",
            "Reverse process subtracts noise to recover images.",
            "It is like un-blurring a photograph.",
            "The image re-emerges from the static."
        ])

        # Assets
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg]
        
        # Animation objects
        noise_box = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg", fill_opacity=0.5, color=WHITE)
        noise_label = Text("Noise", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24)
        noise_group = VGroup(noise_box, noise_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        signal_box = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg", fill_opacity=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        signal_label = Text("Signal", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24)
        signal_group = VGroup(signal_box, signal_label).arrange(DOWN)
        
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(noise_group, 'E2', 'E3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(noise_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(signal_group, 'B2', 'B3', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(FadeIn(signal_group))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'C3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Iterative denoising highlight
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(signal_group, color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        model_label = Text("Diffusion Model", color=WHITE, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(model_label, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)

outline.topic: The Magic of AI Painting: From Text to Pixels
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in AI and mathematics

sections.title: The Core Concept: Diffusion Models (0-1 min)
sections.content: Introduce the forward process (adding Gaussian noise to an image until it is static) and the reverse process (learning to subtract noise to recover the image). Use the metaphor of 'un-blurring a photograph'.
sections.example: Visualizing a clear photo of a Golden Retriever slowly dissolving into white noise, then reversing the animation to show the image 're-emerging' from the static.

sections.title: Bridging Text and Vision: CLIP (1-2 min)
sections.content: Explain how CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) maps text and images into a shared mathematical 'latent space'. If text and image are semantically similar, their vectors are close together.
sections.example: An animation showing a text label 'A cybernetic cat' and an image of a robot-cat being dragged toward each other in a 3D coordinate system, snapping into the same point.

sections.title: The Mathematics: Probability & Gradients (2-3.5 min)
sections.content: Simplify the math: The model predicts a 'noise residual' via a U-Net. We represent the pixel state as a vector 'x'. We use a loss function L = ||ε - ε_θ(x_t, t, context)||², where we minimize the difference between actual noise and predicted noise.
sections.example: A graphical slider showing a 'guidance scale'; moving it changes how strictly the model follows the text prompt versus its own 'imagination' of the image structure.

sections.title: The Synthesis: Putting it Together (3.5-4.5 min)
sections.content: Explain the iterative generation process: CLIP provides the 'direction' (the prompt guidance), and the Diffusion process provides the 'steps' (denoising).
sections.example: A real-time progress bar: at Step 10, the image is a blurry cloud; at Step 50, the sharp details of a steam-punk watch emerge based on the input text.

sections.title: Summary & Future Outlook (4.5-5 min)
sections.content: Recap the synergy: Diffusion models learn the 'structure' of art, while CLIP learns the 'meaning' of language.
sections.example: A final visual of a user typing 'Astronaut on a horse' and the system generating a high-fidelity image in seconds.
